title: Finite scheme quotients for admissible locally finite-type actions over a field
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $V$ be a separated scheme locally of finite type over $e$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let a finite group $H$ act by $e$-scheme automorphisms. Suppose every orbit of underlying points is contained in an affine open of $V$. Then there are an $e$-scheme $Q$ and a finite surjective invariant $e$-morphism $q:V\to Q$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Its geometric fibres are the $H$-orbits [def-weil-geometric-fibre], its underlying map is a topological quotient, and for every open $U\subseteq Q$, the canonical map identifies $\mathcal O_Q(U)$ with $\mathcal O_V(q^{-1}U)^H$. Every invariant morphism from $V$ to a scheme factors uniquely through $q$. On an invariant affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$, the quotient is $\operatorname{Spec}(R^H)$. The scheme $Q$ is locally of finite type over $e$ and is reduced if $V$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The quotient restricts to invariant opens. If $v:V\to B$ is an invariant $e$-morphism and $v^{-1}U\to U$ is finite for an open $U\subseteq B$, then $Q\times_B U\to U$ is finite. Every action on a quasi-projective finite-type $e$-scheme satisfies the orbit-in-an-affine hypothesis, as does every subgroup action. Quasi-projective means a locally closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over $e$ [def-kun-projective]. No faithfulness, freeness, tameness or quasi-compactness of $V$ is required, and no projectivity of $Q$ is asserted.

proof.text: For each orbit $E$, choose an affine open $W$ containing $E$. The finite intersection $W_E=\bigcap_{h\in H}hW$ still contains $E$ and is invariant. Each translate is affine, and repeated application of the separated-affine-intersection lemma over $\operatorname{Spec}e$ shows that $W_E$ is affine. These opens cover $V$. In what follows use the cover consisting of all invariant affine opens, so the argument applies to any such open, not just a selected subcover.

source.place: Tag 01KP, lemma-characterize-separated (1)(a); separatedness simplifies the invariant-neighbourhood input of Tag 03JE

proof.text: Fix an invariant affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and put $A=R^H=\{r:h(r)=r\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. The action groupoid has arrows $\coprod_{h\in H}W$, source $(h,x)\mapsto x$, target $(h,x)\mapsto hx$, inverse $(h,x)\mapsto(h^{-1},hx)$ and composition $(g,hx)\circ(h,x)=(gh,x)$. The group-action identities give its laws. The finite coproduct is $\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_H R)$. The source corresponds to the diagonal $R\to\prod_HR$, whose module has the coordinate basis indexed by $H$, hence is finite locally free; the target is isomorphic to the source via the inverse map. Thus both hypotheses on source and target in the orbit-fibre lemma hold. That lemma says that $p_W:W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is surjective with ordinary and algebraically closed-point fibres precisely the orbits. The finite-invariant-ring lemma says $R$ is integral over $A$; the integral-spectrum closed-map lemma makes $p_W$ closed. It is therefore a topological quotient, and identifies $|W|/H$ homeomorphically with $|\operatorname{Spec}A|$.

source.place: Tag 03BL, lemma-points; finite free action groupoid via 02KB; integrality 0BRI and closedness 00GU/00HZ

proof.text: Define the set $|Q|=|V|/H$ with the quotient topology, and let $q$ be the orbit projection. It is open: the inverse image of the image of an open $O$ is $\bigcup_{h\in H}hO$. For an open $T\subseteq |Q|$ define $\mathcal O_Q(T)=\mathcal O_V(q^{-1}T)^H$ with inherited restriction maps. This is a sheaf of rings: glue matching sections in $\mathcal O_V$ and use uniqueness to see that their glue is fixed by every $h$. The inclusions into $\mathcal O_V(q^{-1}T)$ form a map of sheaves. Every invariant open $W$ is saturated, $q^{-1}q(W)=W$; $q(W)$ is open and carries the orbit-space topology of $W$. For an invariant affine $W$, Step 2 consequently identifies $q(W)$ topologically with $\operatorname{Spec}(R^H)$.

source.place: IX 1.4, pp.132--133, admissible quotient; explicit orbit-space and invariant-sheaf construction supplied here

proof.text: For $A=R^H$ and $f\in A$, the canonical inclusion $A_f\to R_f$ identifies $A_f$ with $(R_f)^H$. Injectivity follows from the fraction equality criterion, since $A\subset R$. For surjectivity, write a fixed fraction as $r/f^n$. For each $h$, fixedness gives an exponent $m_h$ with $f^{m_h}(h(r)-r)=0$. Choose $m$ at least all $m_h$; then $f^mr\in A$ and $r/f^n=(f^mr)/f^{n+m}$. The maps respect restrictions because they are induced by the same inclusions and localization maps. Sections over the inverse image of $D_A(f)$ are $R_f$, by the affine-basic-open section lemma. Hence the canonical map from the structure sheaf of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ to $\mathcal O_Q|_{q(W)}$ is an isomorphism on its basic-open basis. Sheaf gluing gives the isomorphism on every open. Thus $q(W)$ is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $q|_W=p_W$ as a morphism of ringed spaces. These opens cover $Q$, so $Q$ is a scheme and $q$ is a scheme morphism, since the maps $p_W$ are local on stalks. Invariant constants $e\to\mathcal O_Q(T)$ give its $e$-structure; on nonempty stalks the map from the field $e$ is local. This makes $q$ an $e$-morphism.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (3),(5), and 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine; fraction calculation from Algebra 00CO; scheme definition 01IJ

proof.text: The affine opens $q(W)$ have affine inverse images $W$, so the affine-local-target criterion makes $q$ affine. Take any affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Q$. Its inverse image is now affine, say $\operatorname{Spec}R$, and the sheaf definition gives $A=R^H$ under the canonical map. Since $V$ is locally of finite type over $e$, the affine-pairs criterion says $R$ is a finitely generated $e$-algebra. Choose finitely many $e$-algebra generators $r_1,\ldots,r_n$. The same elements generate $R$ over $A$, because the image of $e$ is in $A$. Each is integral over $A$ by the finite-invariant-ring lemma. The finite-integral-adjoining lemma therefore says $R=A[r_1,\ldots,r_n]$ is a finite $A$-module. This holds for every affine $T$, so the definition of a finite morphism proves $q$ finite. Surjectivity and the geometric-point orbit assertion already hold on the cover by $q(W)$ by Step 2, hence hold globally.

source.place: Tag 02JJ, lemma-characterize-finite-in-terms-of-integral (3) => (1), with lemma-characterize-integral; integrality 0BRI; affine-pairs criterion Morphisms 01T2, affine criterion 01S8

proof.text: On each affine $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ just considered, $R$ is finite type over $e$ and finite as an $A$-module. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so Artin--Tate applied to $e\to A\subseteq R$ gives $A$ of finite type over $e$. These affine charts prove $Q$ locally of finite type, with no finite-cover assumption. If $V$ is reduced, every such $R$ is reduced. An element of its subring $A$ with a zero power is zero already in $R$, hence zero in $A$. Thus all affine rings of $Q$ are reduced, which is the reduced-scheme criterion.

Let $a:V\to Z$ be any invariant scheme morphism. Its underlying continuous map factors uniquely through the quotient topology on $|Q|$. For every open $O\subseteq Z$, $a^\sharp$ takes values in $\mathcal O_V(a^{-1}O)^H$, since $a\circ h=a$ as scheme morphisms, so it factors through $\mathcal O_Q$ and defines a ringed-space morphism $b:Q\to Z$. This factor is local: for $y\in Q$ choose $x$ above it. If a germ in the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{Z,b(y)}$ mapped to a unit at $y$, its pullback would be a unit at $x$, contradicting locality of $a$. Thus $b$ is a scheme morphism. Uniqueness follows from surjectivity on points and the inclusions of section rings. In particular invariant $e$-morphisms factor by $e$-morphisms, since the two structure composites agree after $q$. The construction on any invariant open $V'\subseteq V$ is literally the restriction of the orbit space and invariant sheaf to $q(V')$. It proves the same universal property there, and Step 4, applied to every invariant affine, gives exactly the asserted affine quotient formula.

source.place: IX 1.4, pp.132--133, and X 2.3 Step 2, p.151; explicit categorical and invariant-open verification supplied here

proof.text: For the finiteness assertion over $U\subseteq B$, let $b:Q\to B$ be the factor of $v$ from Step 7. Fix an affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $U$. Finiteness of $v^{-1}U\to U$ gives an affine $W=v^{-1}T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a finite $C$-module. It is invariant, so Steps 3--4 give $b^{-1}T=q(W)=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A=R^H$. The image $C'\subseteq R$ of $C$ is contained in $A$ because $v$ is invariant, and it contains the image of $e$ because $v$ is an $e$-morphism. The same finite module generators show $R$ is finite over $C'$. The affine-pairs criterion makes $R$ finite type over $e$. Artin--Tate applied to $e\to C'\subseteq R$ gives $C'$ of finite type over $e$. This uses no Noetherian assumption on $C$ or on $B$.

source.place: Tag 00IS, lemma-Artin-Tate, applied to the image subalgebra of the arbitrary base section ring

proof.text: The finite-type Noetherian-ring lemma makes $C'$ Noetherian. Regard $A\subseteq R$ as a $C'$-submodule; it is stable because $C'\subseteq A$. Since $R$ is finite over $C'$, the Noetherian-submodule lemma makes $A$ finite over $C'$. Those same generators generate $A$ over $C$, since $C\to C'$ is onto. Consequently $b^{-1}T\to T$ is finite for every affine open $T$ of $U$. By the definition of a finite morphism, $Q\times_B U=b^{-1}U\to U$ is finite. The equality denotes the usual canonical identification of the inverse image of an open with its fibre product.

source.place: Tags 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, and 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic; Morphisms finite definition

proof.text: Finally suppose $V$ has a locally closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_e=\operatorname{Proj}S$, $S=e[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$. Factor it as a closed immersion into an open $O$ of $\operatorname{Proj}S$. For a finite nonempty subset $E\subseteq V$, write the complement of $O$ as $V_+(J)$ for a homogeneous ideal $J$, and let $I=J\cap S_+$. For each homogeneous prime corresponding to a point of $E$, $I$ is not contained in that prime: $J$ is not contained in it and neither is $S_+$, so the product of a member of each outside the prime belongs to $I$ and is outside it. Graded prime avoidance supplies a positive-degree homogeneous $f\in I$ missing all those primes. Then $D_+(f)$ is affine, contains the image of $E$ and is contained in $O$. Its inverse image in $V$ is affine, by the affine description of a closed immersion, and contains $E$. The empty set is contained in the empty affine open. In particular every finite-group orbit lies in an affine open. Every subgroup orbit is a subset of the corresponding whole-group orbit, so the same assertion holds for subgroup actions (indeed this last observation holds for any admissible action).
